title: Senate Map Widens Into Final Week Before Nov. 3 Midterms
dek: Toss-up races now stretch into Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio and Texas heading into Nov. 3, and counting disputes in some races could run for weeks.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The west front of the United States Capitol building in Washington, D.C.

keyPoints: NPR reports the competitive Senate map has expanded considerably in the final days, with races in states Trump won by double digits in 2024 now within the margin of error.
The Cook Political Report rates Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio and Texas as toss-ups, according to NPR.
Election Day is Nov. 3. Early-voting calendars are set state by state; an Oct. 13-30 window cited in NPR's coverage refers to Georgia, not the whole country.
Reuters reports some races may take weeks to clear recounts and court challenges, and that Congress has the final say on contested outcomes.
body:
The final week of the 2026 midterm campaign has pushed the Senate battlefield well beyond the seats Democrats were expected to defend or target at the start of the cycle. NPR reported on Friday that the competitive map has expanded considerably as the war with Iran has continued, putting races in states Trump carried by double digits in 2024 within the margin of error.

## The toss-ups

The Cook Political Report rates Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio and Texas as toss-ups, NPR reported. The chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand of New York, told NPR the party had "so many candidates running in so many deep red and purple places" and that those candidates were winning. Republicans disputed that picture; the National Republican Senatorial Committee accused Democrats of misconduct in the Alaska race, a claim NPR reported without resolution.

## Calendar and counting

Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Early-voting rules and deadlines differ by state; the Oct. 13-30 early-voting period that appears in NPR's coverage describes voting in Georgia, shown at a library in East Point, near Atlanta, and is not a national calendar. Voters should check their own state's election office for deadlines.

Reuters reported that some races may take weeks to clear recounts and court challenges, and that Congress ultimately has the final say on contested outcomes. The Senate result will be read against the House map in the days after Tuesday.

Forecasts can shift quickly in the final days, and this story is a snapshot of reporting available on Oct. 30. It will be updated as results and any recount or court actions come in.

## What to watch

The five toss-up states named by Cook are the clearest guide to where control of the Senate will be decided. Because several of them are states Trump won comfortably in 2024, a close result in any one of them would itself be a signal about the national mood after months of war with Iran. Results in close contests may not be known on election night: the Reuters explainer notes that recounts and legal challenges can stretch on, and that contested outcomes ultimately come before Congress.

*Correction, Oct. 30: An earlier version of this story presented Georgia's Oct. 13-30 early-voting period as a nationwide calendar and repeated several passages. It has been corrected.*
